- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–4% if recent price is trending down.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior 5-day avg), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 7 days.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day mean, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% per day until price stabilizes.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model may misread momentum; align forecast with sentiment swing direction, not absolute trend.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from model, check if sentiment was neutral or negative 3–5 days prior — if so, model likely missed downward bias.
